approved: 2026-11-21: segment acceptance thresholds approved by the product owner (Ambiguous redefined as 'correct handling of ambiguity')
nature: Operational acceptance thresholds for evaluation version 1. They are NOT claims of statistically validated product performance.
principle: Every gate is evaluated SEPARATELY per language (Arabic, English) and, for segment gates, per segment. A gate passes only if it passes in EVERY language (and segment) it applies to. Aggregate or pooled figures are reported for information only and can never compensate for a failed language-specific or segment-specific gate. Missing required evidence (no data, denominator 0, judge not calibrated) = gate not passed = NO-GO; nothing is ever assumed to pass.

statistics.unit: scenario-run (each held-out scenario is run R times; R = 2 by default)
statistics.estimate: mean over scenarios of each scenario's per-run success rate (equals the run-level rate when every scenario has the same number of eligible runs)
statistics.ci95: Wilson 95% interval computed on the number of DISTINCT scenarios (effective n), not on runs, because repeated runs of one scenario are not independent
statistics.threshold_pass: point estimate meets the threshold → the operational gate passes (this alone decides the gate)
statistics.statistically_established: for '>=': CI lower bound ≥ threshold; for '<=': CI upper bound ≤ threshold. Reported separately; it is NOT required for the gate and is expected to be 'no' for most gates at Phase 0 sample sizes

segments.definition: clear = the seven requested business categories; ambiguous = category 'ambiguous'; incomplete_information = expected gate 'ask'; outside_catalogue = no-good-fit cases whose expected domains do not include X.OUT_OF_SCOPE; out_of_scope = expected domain X.OUT_OF_SCOPE or category out_of_scope

segment_acceptance.label: Clear: correct first framework recommendation
segment_acceptance.numerator: clear scenario-runs where status = ok (recommendations shown) AND the rank-1 approach ∈ expected ideal ∪ acceptable (Gantt ≡ Action Plan)
segment_acceptance.denominator: all clear scenario-runs (asking, declining or 'no good fit' on a clear case counts as not correct)

segment_acceptance.label: Ambiguous: correct handling of ambiguity (a single framework is NOT required)
segment_acceptance.numerator: ambiguous scenario-runs with NO unacceptable approach displayed AND status ∉ {no_good_fit, out_of_scope} AND at least one of: (a) clarification — status = insufficient_context with ≥ 1 identified missing item (unknowns); (b) acceptable recommendation — status = ok and rank-1 ∈ ideal ∪ acceptable; (c) conditional/alternative interpretation — status = ok, the model rated its rank-1 fit below 'high' (signalled uncertainty) and the displayed top 3 contains an approach in ideal ∪ acceptable
segment_acceptance.note: Whether conditional recommendations state their assumptions explicitly is not machine-checkable; the blinded human evaluator's 'next step' rating on sampled ambiguous cases is reported alongside as supporting evidence (does not change the gate)

segment_acceptance.label: Clear + Ambiguous: unsuitable framework appearing in the displayed top 3
segment_acceptance.numerator: clear+ambiguous scenario-runs with status = ok whose displayed top 3 contains an approach in the scenario's expected 'unacceptable' list
segment_acceptance.denominator: clear+ambiguous scenario-runs with status = ok (recommendations actually displayed); denominator 0 = missing evidence → NO-GO
segment_acceptance.per: evaluated per language over the combined clear+ambiguous rows, AND reported per segment

segment_acceptance.label: Incomplete information: requests the necessary information before any definitive recommendation
segment_acceptance.numerator: incomplete-information scenario-runs with status = insufficient_context (no recommendation displayed) AND ≥ 1 identified missing item (unknowns)

segment_acceptance.label: Outside catalogue: correctly identifies AND communicates 'No Good Fit'
segment_acceptance.numerator: outside-catalogue scenario-runs with status = no_good_fit AND a non-empty user-facing no-good-fit explanation
segment_acceptance.note: Strict: when the deterministic rule decides No Good Fit, the frozen eval-v1 harness does not call the model to write the explanation, so such runs count as NOT communicated. 'Identified but not communicated' is reported separately. If this causes a failure it is a NO-GO; fixing the harness requires evaluation version 2

segment_acceptance.label: Out of scope: correctly declines or redirects
segment_acceptance.numerator: out-of-scope scenario-runs with status ∈ {out_of_scope (declined), no_good_fit (redirected: no method offered)}; any displayed recommendation = fail

additional_acceptance.approved: 2026-11-21 (Option B): separate acceptance metric; the six segment gates S1–S6 are unchanged
additional_acceptance.label: Conditional Recommendation Assumption Integrity
additional_acceptance.eligible: ambiguous scenario-runs where a conditional recommendation was actually provided: status = ok, ≥ 1 recommendation displayed, and the model rated its rank-1 fit below 'high'. Clarification requests, No Good Fit, declines and unconditional (high-fit) recommendations are NOT eligible and are not penalised (lib/assumption-integrity.mjs eligibility)
additional_acceptance.numerator: eligible scenario-runs where the calibrated AI judge answers 'yes' to ALL three criteria: AI1 assumptions the recommendation depends on are explicitly stated; AI2 every assumption relied on is supported by the case information or clearly labelled unverified; AI3 it explains how the recommendation would change if the assumptions prove incorrect ('partial' does not pass)
additional_acceptance.denominator: all eligible scenario-runs (per language). Denominator 0, any eligible run without a complete judge verdict, or a judge not calibrated for that language → not established → NO-GO
additional_acceptance.measured_by: scripts/assumption-judge.mjs (AI judge on stored experiment-A outputs; judge model and Judge schema imported unchanged from the frozen config)

per_language.numerator: runs whose model stage ∈ expected stage_any_of
runs whose top domain ∈ expected domains (any-of ∪ acceptable)
runs with status ok and rank-1 ∈ ideal ∪ acceptable
per_language.change_2026_11_21: applies to clear only (was clear+ambiguous); ambiguous is governed by S2 so that clarification is never penalised

per_language.numerator: runs with status ok and an ideal approach in the top 3
runs with status no_good_fit or out_of_scope

per_language.change_2026_11_21: applies to clear only (was clear+ambiguous): asking on an ambiguous case is acceptable handling

per_language.numerator: user-attributed statements without a verbatim quote
model recommendations outside the rule-approved candidates

cross_language.note: Gap between Arabic and English 'case correct' rates, where case correct = the segment acceptance criterion of the case's own segment (S1/S2/S4/S5/S6). Additional to, never instead of, the per-language gates

per_language.numerator: option sets passing the structural checks
option sets judged free of fabricated facts
critical/high findings matching a seeded defect
critic runs where every finding has an explanation and a correction
calls with usage but no parsed output

per_language.coverage: every eligible judged case rated blind by the human evaluator
per_language.note: per language; separate from the checklist gate; required before S7 can pass; adjudication of all disagreements must be complete

calibration.per_criterion: Reported for every criterion × language with n, agreement and Cohen's kappa; n < 10 flagged 'insufficient sample'.

pptx.rule: Workbook exit criteria met, recomputed from cell values (doc 16 §6)

go_rule: GO only if ALL of: every prerequisite present (held-out runs A, B, C; S7 assumption-integrity judge run on that A run; measured cost/latency F; human calibration completed and adjudicated; PowerPoint workbook complete) AND every approved gate passes in Arabic AND in English AND every segment gate S1–S6 passes in each language AND S7 (conditional assumption integrity, calibrated judge) passes in each language AND the cross-language gate passes AND the PowerPoint exit criteria are met. Anything else → NO-GO.
